bullets.title: NVDA: Wells Fargo reiterates OW, $315 PT on $500B+ AI infrastructure financing
bullets.body: Wells Fargo maintained its Overweight rating on NVDA with a $315 price target, citing NVIDIA's partnership with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR on a $500B+ AI infrastructure financing program. One commentator noted this 'bank of Nvidia' creates a 'protective financing moat' while raising credit risk concerns given commitments against finite free cash flow. Jensen Huang separately characterized the move as transitioning NVIDIA from chipmaker to 'creator of a new investable asset class.'

bullets.title: TSM: TSMC CoWoS capacity doubled 3 years running; Sony JV announced for $4.7B
bullets.body: TSMC VP Jun He confirmed CoWoS capacity has doubled annually for three consecutive years, with 10 advanced packaging plants now operating and 5.5x reticle-size CoWoS in mass production at over 98% yields—though demand is still not fully satisfied. Separately, TSMC and Sony officially announced the 'Advanced Vision' JV in Kumamoto, Japan, with combined investment of $4.7B (Sony contributing $2.92B as controlling shareholder, TSMC $1.77B), targeting volume production of next-gen smartphone image sensors in 2029.

bullets.title: SNDK: 40% selloff seen as overdone given 300-400% revenue growth guide and $4.5B buybacks
bullets.body: SNDK fell from ~$2,000 to ~$1,200, but fintwit notes Q1 FY27 guidance points to 300-400% revenue growth, ~$45 adjusted EPS, zero debt, and $4.5B in buybacks executed last quarter. The thesis: while revenue growth is decelerating, fundamentals remain strong and the selloff is characterized as a panic overreaction.

bullets.title: INTC: Raises $20B in upsized share sale at $95/share, 6.5% discount
bullets.body: Intel priced an upsized share offering at $95/share—a 6.5% discount to prior close—raising $20B, well above the initial $15B target. The deal's scale signals significant capital needs and potential dilution pressure.

bullets.title: AAPL/GLW: Glass-centric 20th-anniversary iPhone on track, countering Jefferies downgrade
bullets.body: Sources cited on fintwit indicate Apple's glass-centric design for its 2027 20th-anniversary iPhone remains on track, directly pushing back on the Jefferies downgrade thesis on AAPL. Corning (GLW) flagged as a relevant beneficiary as the glass supplier for the design.

bullets.title: TSEM: 5.5x reticle CoWoS in mass production with 98%+ yields across multiple AI clients
bullets.body: Tower Semiconductor (TSEM) is highlighted as achieving over 98% yields on 5.5x reticle-size CoWoS in mass production across multiple AI client products, signaling a significant ramp ahead for advanced packaging revenue.

bullets.title: ABF substrate shortage seen as second-biggest supply bottleneck after memory
bullets.body: Fintwit semiconductor analysts flag ABF substrate shortages as the next major supply constraint behind memory, with companies already diversifying sourcing across multiple suppliers. Variations in thermal and mechanical properties across suppliers are cited as an operational challenge during the diversification process.

bullets.title: NFLX briefly dipped below 200-week moving average for first time in 3 years, then recovered
bullets.body: NFLX broke below its 200-week moving average—a technically significant level not breached in three years—but quickly reclaimed it, which technicians on fintwit view as a bullish recovery signal.

bullets.title: NVDA AI bubble cracks flagged; High Beta Momentum down 3.7% while SPY barely moves
bullets.body: One macro commentator notes 'The AI Bubble Is Cracking In Places Nobody's Watching,' while Hedgeye data showed High Beta Momentum down 3.7% on the day versus SPY -0.1%, with retail investors chasing AI headlines losing -1.0%. Post-close NVDA $500B deal storytelling is characterized as narrative-driven rather than fundamental.

bullets.title: GPU market at $1.5T by 2028 requires ASPs to 3x—current economics questioned
bullets.body: A fintwit semiconductor analyst argues that hitting a $1.5T GPU market by 2028 requires GPU average selling prices to triple and FLOPS/$ efficiency to improve rather than decline, questioning whether current GPU economics can support the scale implied by consensus forecasts.

bullets.title: Macro: NFIB Small Business Optimism surges to 99.8, highest since Aug 2023; labor quality tops concerns
bullets.body: July NFIB Small Business Optimism hit 99.8 vs. 97.5 estimate and 97.4 prior—the highest reading since August 2023. Labor quality displaced all other concerns as the single most important problem, rising 8 percentage points month-over-month and running 15pp above the historical average of 12%; inflation concerns eased.

bullets.title: Macro: Brent crude near $90/bbl (+$10 in a week) on Iran/Hormuz tensions; oil then reverses on peace signals
bullets.body: Brent crude rallied toward $90/barrel—up $10 in a week—driven by Trump's tough Iran stance and Hormuz concerns, pushing Treasury yields and the dollar higher and lifting September Fed rate hike odds to 44%. Oil subsequently turned negative intraday after Pakistan's defense minister signaled the US and Iran are 'close to some arrangement,' with Qatar confirming Oman-Iran negotiations are in an advanced stage.

bullets.title: Macro: Yield curve steepens to +47bps on 10s-2s; bonds short signal intact
bullets.body: The 10s-2s yield curve steepened to a new Quad3 high of +47bps, with at least one macro strategist maintaining long steepener positions and staying short TLT and LQD. Reuters poll separately forecasts 10Y yields easing to 4.34% and 2Y to 3.80% over 12 months.

bullets.title: Macro: HSBC flags Wednesday CPI as potential dovish catalyst; NY Fed inflation expectations edge down
bullets.body: HSBC expects another benign July CPI print following June's softer-than-expected reading, which could push rate hike pricing further out. NY Fed survey showed 1-year and 3-year inflation expectations edged down in July; consensus CPI estimate is +3.4% headline and +2.5% core. Separately, one fintwit account warned headline CPI may look benign but underlying components could show hidden deterioration.

bullets.title: Macro: Labor force participation hits 61.4%, lowest since early 2021; BofA cites wealth effect
bullets.body: US labor force participation fell to 61.4% in July, its lowest since early 2021. BofA attributes the decline among 55+ Americans (participation now 36.9%, down from 40%+ pre-pandemic) primarily to early retirement driven by stock market wealth gains—a dynamic multiple fintwit accounts flagged as contributing to labor quality shortages cited by small businesses.

bullets.title: S&P 500 EPS tracking 32% growth in Q2, but BofA warns slowdown to mid-teens by 2027
bullets.body: S&P 500 EPS is tracking 32% growth in Q2 following 30% in Q1—historically rare back-to-back 30%+ quarters—but BofA warns growth could decelerate below 20% by Q1 2027 and to mid-teens for full-year 2027, setting up potential valuation pressure.

bullets.title: Red Sea/Gulf of Oman: Multiple shipping incidents signal elevated geopolitical risk to tanker routes
bullets.body: UKMTO reported a cargo vessel struck by projectile near Yemen/al-Mokha with casualties, a separate tanker incident in the Gulf of Oman involving military forces, and Yemeni forces targeting a Saudi commercial ship in Bab-el-Mandeb—all within the same morning window, flagging persistent pressure on key energy shipping lanes.

bullets.title: France 30Y bond yield hits 4.80%, highest since Oct 2008; eurozone fiscal stress rising
bullets.body: France's 30-year bond yield rose 3bps to 4.8004%, the highest level since October 2008, reflecting growing eurozone fiscal concerns alongside Germany facing energy price pressures from low Rhine/hydroelectric water levels.

bullets.title: US SPR at 40-year lows; debt servicing costs up 200% in five years
bullets.body: Two separate fintwit posts highlight structural US macro vulnerabilities: strategic petroleum reserves depleted to levels not seen in four decades, and debt-servicing payments up 200% over five years as elevated interest rates compound fiscal stress.

bullets.title: Consumer credit rebounds $14.2B in June; BNPL adoption for groceries reaches ~10% of adults
bullets.body: Consumer credit rose $14.2B in June (revolving +$6.7B, non-revolving +$7.4B) after an unusual $1.1B decline in May, suggesting resilient consumer spending. Separately, nearly 1 in 10 US adults have used buy-now-pay-later services for grocery purchases, pointing to stress in lower-income consumer segments.
